![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943521/assets/39d3bd73ac0f60f21cc9e71cbf46d62901fcc07cab3b06cd84a496b1e1415a1a.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx)+D,$ where $B$ and $D$ are constants. What is $B+D?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The period $T$ of the function is

$$
T=\frac{2\pi }{3}.
$$

The formula for the period $T$ of the function $y=A\operatorname{cot}⁡(Bx+C)+D$ is given by 

$$
T=\frac{\pi }{B}.
$$

Applying the formula of the period, we get

$$
\frac{2\pi }{3}=\frac{\pi }{B}\,⟹\,B=\frac{\pi }{(\frac{2\pi }{3})}=\frac{3}{2}.
$$

The parameter $D$ represents the vertical shift of the cotangent function. We see that the function has been translated by $5$ units down. Hence, $D=-5.$

Therefore, $B+D=\frac{3}{2}+(-5)=-\frac{7}{2}.$

Finally, the equation of the curve is

$$
y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3x}{2})-5.
$$
